sense.text:
“Thou givest thy mouth to evil” is speaking of Esau, the white man. He gives his mouth to evil and speaks much evil against God and against God’s people.

“And thy tongue frameth deceit”: he speaks lies and calls himself a Jew.

“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother”: he speaks against the 12 tribes of Israel, against the negroes, the blacks and the Hispanics. The white man always speaks against us. Always.

“Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”: he lies on us, his own brother.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: the white man has done all these things, and God kept silent. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: he thinks God is like him, unjust like him.

“But I will reprove thee.” God is going to reprove the nation of Edom, the so-called white man, and it is already going on right now: the wars in Russia and Ukraine with all those people dying, the rioting in France, all the things happening all over Europe. This is the time we are living in, when God is reproving the white man for all the lies and all the evil he has done and spoken against us.

“And set them in order before thine eyes.” As God judges Edom, he sets the 12 tribes of Israel in order right before his eyes. We need to be set in order because our people do not understand order. We are not of one mind; we are divided and we do not understand working together. Negroes are always late for everything, even for tabernacles. That is going to stop. God is going to put his spirit on the brothers that fear him, and they will start taking things serious: structure and order in your life, in your house, and in the nation of Israel.

Esau thought he destroyed us. Esau said, these negroes can’t do nothing, they can’t work together, they can’t even be on time for a damn job, colored people time, they cannot organize. That is the evil he speaks in the verses above. But God says, you destroyed my people so that they don’t understand order, but I will set them in order right before your eyes.

God does it by sending men, and it starts first and foremost with the bishops. They set up order and structure in IUIC, and we all follow that order and build on top of it. It trickles down to the brothers over the offices, the medical team, security, and the brothers that organize the feast of tabernacles for thousands of brothers and sisters all over the country, men God has put his spirit on. As men of God we have to stop doing and saying whatever we want. The kingdom of heaven is about order and structure, and that order being established is what you are seeing happen right now.

“Therefore will I cast you out of this land”: we were cast out of the land of Israel. That is our land. It does not belong to the Palestinians, and it does not belong to these Europeans that call themselves Jews.

“Into a land that ye know not, neither ye nor your fathers”: we never knew about America and all these lands we were brought into. “And there shall ye serve other gods day and night”: you worship the white man, you worship the Arab man, you follow Christianity.

“Where I will not shew you favour.” We will have no favor here in Babylon, the land of our captivity. If some of you think things are going to get better for the negro living here, God says that in that land he will show you no favor.

It will no more be said, “The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt”, but “The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north”. The land of the north is the United States of America, North America: Babylon, Mystery Babylon the great. God delivers the children of Israel from America.

“And from all the lands whither he had driven them”: every land our people were driven to, whether Africa, the islands or the South Pacific, wherever we were scattered. “And I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is what deliverance is about, and what the rapture is about: being brought back into our land. The same deliverance that took place in ancient Egypt will take place in spiritual Egypt, which is America.

That is where the feast of tabernacles is going. It will not be said that we dwelt in booths coming out of Egypt, but that we were delivered from the land of the north and dwelt in booths after we came out of it. That will be the new feast day: tabernacles honored in the future as the deliverance from America, the deliverance from Babylon.
“As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you.” This is what the Christians call the rapture.

“And I will bring you out from the people.” The people are the white people here in America, all the mixed multitude here. God is going to bring us out from among the people.

“And will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered.” He is not gathering all nations here. He says you, the children of Israel, I am going to gather from all these countries. “With fury poured out”: that fury poured out is Armageddon. That is the time Christ is going to deliver us.

“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people.” The Lord is taking us out of America and back into the wilderness, most likely that same wilderness we were in before. When we are delivered from the destruction here, you are not going to be floating around in the sky; you are going to be taken into the wilderness.

And when we go back into the wilderness, we will be dwelling in booths, in tabernacles, again. We are not going to be just walking around in the sand; we will be building booths and tents and dwelling there, and Christ will set us in order right there.

“And there will I plead with you face to face.” He will plead with us, and teach us, face to face.

“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you.” The same way he pleaded with our forefathers in the wilderness when he brought them out of Egypt, he will do it to us again.

“And I will cause you to pass under the rod”: the rod is correction. “And I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.” We are under the new covenant, but are we under the bond of the new covenant? He brings us into it by teaching us, and by killing the rebellious of our people.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me.” Christ brings us into the wilderness, but there will still be rebels among us, rebellious brothers and sisters, those that transgress against the Lord. God will get rid of all of them, and this takes place in the wilderness while we are dwelling in booths again. A brother from New York asked how long we will be there, forty years again? We don’t know how long, but we are going back into the wilderness, Christ will be teaching us, and the rebels among us will be put to death.

“I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn”: some people will be delivered up out of Babylon, the chariot will beam you up. “And they shall not enter into the land of Israel.” You go into the wilderness, but you do not enter the land. It is the same thing that was done back then: our forefathers did not enter the land; God killed off that whole generation. The same thing will be done again.

Everything we celebrate has a meaning behind it. We celebrate the feast of tabernacles because we will dwell in tabernacles again. Some of you are saying, damn, it’s cold out here, no cellular network, no Wi-Fi, you lost the comforts of your home. It is going back to the same thing. This is preparation; we are rehearsing the righteous acts. Some of your spirits are not right. Get your spirit right.

“And ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

precepts.why:
This is the bond of the covenant: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God.”

In the bond of the new covenant we are going to learn God’s laws, understand everything plainly, and not sin again. That is why we have to pass under the rod first. The rod is correction, and a lot of people are going to die. Where? In the wilderness, where we will be dwelling in tabernacles, in booths, again.

“And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him.” The one they pierced is Christ our king. This takes place when we are delivered up out of here, most likely in the wilderness.

This is the first time we see the Lord. Remember, Ezekiel says he will plead with us face to face. When we see him in the wilderness we will mourn for him “as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.” “In that day”, in the wilderness, “shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem”.

“And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart”, of Levi and of Shimei. When Christ returns you are going to know what family you are from. The Lord is going to make everything plain.

We will mourn because we understand he was stricken because of us. We are the ones that delivered him up to the Romans; we said crucify him, crucify him. We will mourn when we see him and see the wounds in his hands, in the wilderness, while we are building booths and tents and dwelling there, and Christ sets us in order, purges out the rebels, and teaches us face to face.

“In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.” That fountain is Christ.

“I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered.” That day is in the wilderness, when he purges out the rebels, brings us under the bond of the covenant and teaches us face to face, while we are back in the wilderness dwelling in booths. You are not going to be worshipping white Jesus no more, or Allah no more. Whatever idolatrous things our people follow, knowingly or unknowingly, the Lord is going to cut out and say, stop doing that, that’s wrong. Some of you argue with us when we tell you to stop that baby shower crap. In that day the Lord will teach you face to face.

“And also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land”: no more unclean spirits and no more false prophets among us.

“Then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the Lord: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.” If you have a son speaking lies, opening his mouth in the wilderness, he is going to be put to death, and the mother and the father have to do it. This is the wilderness, while we are dwelling in booths. We do this every year, come together and dwell in tabernacles, and it is going to happen again in the future.

sense.text:
“Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem.” All nations took part in destroying us. Those that are left are the people not destroyed at Armageddon, when Christ destroys the nations: the people the Lord saved to be slaves.

They “shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” When Christ is ruling, for that thousand years, the nations will be here serving Christ and the Israelites. When God is ruling, the nations will not be here. Those that have ears to hear, let them hear.

They come up to keep the feast of tabernacles because we will be celebrating tabernacles in the kingdom when Christ returns, since when we are delivered we will be dwelling in tabernacles again. They are not coming into the city; they will be outside the city, coming up to honor us and to worship our king. They will be forced. You think these Chinese are going to willingly worship a black man? No. They have to see his power first and feel it. But the whole earth is going to worship Christ, and the Father.

“Whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.” They will die from famine: no rain, no food, no crops. That is the judgment. When Christ returns the nations will come up and honor Christ and the Israelites while we celebrate the feast of tabernacles, and if they don’t come up, they will die.

“If the family of Egypt go not up”, “there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.” All the heathen that do not come up to us at tabernacles, the Lord is going to plague. Salvation is not for everyone in the sense you are thinking. The kingdom of heaven is a hierarchy: the Israelites ruling this earth in righteousness under Christ for a thousand years.

“This shall be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all nations that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.” This shows that salvation is not for all nations. All nations will be subjected unto us.

precepts.why:
The nations will be in the kingdom, but they will be forced to worship the Lord. Salvation is not designed for them. But the dogs get crumbs too: they can pray, and their prayers will be answered. The Lord first and foremost is dealing with his people.

“The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains.” Black people, what you call black and Hispanics today, will be established above every nation on this earth. If we endure and keep these commandments, we are going to rule everything.

“And all nations shall flow unto it.” The Arabs that are left, the Chinese that are left, the so-called Hamitic tribes that are left, Ammon that is left: all nations are going to flow unto us, after that nuclear war, after Christ comes back and destroys America and Europe. It is going to happen whether you believe it or not. We will rule this earth with our king.

“Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people.” This has to happen before the verses above: many people have to be judged and rebuked. Some white people will think they can test us, test the Israelites, test Christ, and they will be rebuked and judged. Only then “they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”: their weapons of war turned into farming equipment.

sense.text: “All our fathers were under the cloud.” The people Paul is speaking to are Israelites, Israel that was scattered in Corinth, not heathens, because all of their fathers were under the cloud and “passed through the sea”.
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: Moses taught all our fathers.
“They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Christ followed them in the wilderness.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” God was not pleased with our forefathers in the wilderness. Even Moses: he was righteous, but he made a mistake, and the Lord said, you will not see the land.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” God delivered them from Egypt and they started lusting after evil things.

Why is it our example? Because Paul understood Ezekiel 20: we are going right back into the wilderness. When you celebrate tabernacles, the feast of booths, you are rehearsing what you will do in the future when Christ returns. Everything that happened to our forefathers in the wilderness is an example for us not to do the same thing.

So at the feast of tabernacles, stay in the spirit. There should be no funny business, no murmuring and no speaking evil against each other. Those that came to tabernacles last year being evil and causing confusion are going to be the same ones that are the rebels in the wilderness, because we are supposed to be rehearsing the righteous acts. If you can’t get it right now, you think you’re going to get it right when Christ returns?
“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” They were partying, having orgies, and worshipping an idol, Bacchus.
“Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” 23,000.
“Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.” It was Christ in the wilderness that they tempted, and they were destroyed by serpents.
“Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.” Don’t murmur as some of them murmured.

precepts.why:
This is where they rose up to play. “And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings”: offerings to the calf, an idol. That is what the children of Israel did, that is what we did, after we saw God and were delivered from ancient Egypt.

“And the people sat down to eat and to drink”: we cooked food and were eating, drinking and getting drunk. “And rose up to play”: we were fornicating, having sex orgies, sexual immorality. That is what we did when we came out.

You young brothers and young sisters, don’t be on that foolishness. If you can’t get it right now, you’re not going to get it right when the Lord delivers us up out of here.

“And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” They started banging Chinese women. I don’t know why you brothers are lusting after the Chinese woman; she ain’t got no butt.

“And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.” The Chinese woman had you worshipping Buddha, bowing down to their gods and eating their food offered to Buddha. “And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor”: you joined yourself unto that which was against your own people. “And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

“And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.” The Lord said, chop off their heads and hang them up so I can see it. That is how bad the Lord is: everybody that worships idols and turns against him, cut off their heads, and only that will turn his anger away. And Moses said to the judges, “Slay ye every one his men”.

That is what happened in the wilderness, and in Ezekiel the same thing is going to happen again: the Lord brings us back into the wilderness, we dwell in booths again, he brings us under the bond of the covenant and purges out the rebels from among us. That is why Paul said this happened for our example.

A man of Israel brought “a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses”, while the congregation was weeping “before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.” Phinehas “took a javelin in his hand”, went after them into the tent “and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.” “And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.”

24,000 people died. Get it together: the murmuring, the speaking evil, the fornication. If you don’t get it right, the Lord may have mercy and bring you into the wilderness, but you are not going to enter the promised land.

Neither murmur, as they murmured and were destroyed of the destroyer: “And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.” They said, why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the wilderness; we’re hungry; our soul hates this bread.

You think the same thing won’t happen? Some of you will miss Popeyes chicken and McDonald’s. There will be no more Popeyes chicken, no more McDonald’s, no more of this junk nasty food you eat, and you will murmur and talk crap at that time.

“And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.” They were murmuring against Moses and against the Lord, and the Lord sent serpents and destroyed them. Then the people said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us.” Speaking against God and speaking against Moses: that is murmuring, speaking evil.

All of this is the wilderness. Paul said learn from our forefathers’ example in the wilderness, because we are going right back into the wilderness and dwelling in booths again. And Christ gives an analogy of what is going to happen when we are back there.

“For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard. And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.” Why are we all serving God, laboring in the vineyard, learning to love each other and do right by each other? Because God promised us the kingdom. The Lord called us and sent us to labor, and our reward, our hire, is the kingdom of heaven.

“Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.” Some came in early and some came in last, but all of them get their hire, the kingdom. “They received every man a penny.” “But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more”. Some brothers are going to say, I did more work than him, why is he over me? Negroes murmur, and we will be murmuring again.

“They murmured against the goodman of the house”: they are going to murmur against Christ. That is what Paul was warning us about. “These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.” I was in the streets of Babylon teaching the word while nuclear bombs were dropping; I spent five years in jail teaching the truth; I did more; why is he over me?

“Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?” All of us wanted the kingdom. “Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.” “Is thine eye evil, because I am good? So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.”

This is in the wilderness, where the Lord says, I will purge out from among you the rebels. You got delivered, you got the penny, and you are complaining. Train your mind to stop murmuring now, because if you don’t get it right now, you will do it again when the Lord returns.

By the time we get the kingdom, everybody is going to be righteous. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

Those enemies are the same rebellious brothers and sisters in the wilderness. Not wanting him to reign over them means not wanting to listen to the men Christ set up. If the Lord told Peter to put an order out and you don’t want to listen to Peter, you don’t want the Lord to rule over you, and he says bring them here and kill them before me.

This is a future prophecy of the wilderness while we are dwelling in tabernacles: the Lord bringing us under the bond of the covenant and purging out the rebels from among us. There will be a lot of rebellion in the wilderness. That is why you had better train yourself right now, at tabernacles. And have joy.

sense.text: “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days”: don’t let nobody judge you concerning the holy days, the new moons or the sabbaths.
“Which are a shadow of things to come.” Every high holy day is a shadow of things to come. When we celebrate tabernacles and dwell in booths, it is a shadow of something to come.

precepts.why:
“Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” There are wondrous things written in the law, even in the feast of tabernacles and the way we celebrate it, but you need God to open your eyes so you can behold the wondrous things out of the laws we keep.

The Lord did not command you to keep the sabbath day for no reason, and he did not command you to keep the feast of tabernacles for no reason. There are reasons behind every high holy day we celebrate.

sense.text: “Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” They are the Lord’s feasts.
“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, “it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.” The seventh day sabbath is the Lord’s sabbath.

precepts.why: “For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” The Son of man is Christ, and Christ is Lord of the sabbath day, meaning the sabbath was created for him. That is why Leviticus 23 says “it is the sabbath of the Lord”: it is the Lord’s sabbath.
“I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day.” The sabbath day is the Lord’s day.

“For we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest”. The rest is the sabbath, and it is his rest. But it uses an action word: we “enter into rest”. When Christ is Lord of the sabbath, and the Lord rested on the seventh day, it is not talking about a day. It is talking about a place you enter into.

When Genesis says God rested, people say, why would God rest, was he tired? He was not tired; he did not tell the angels, I’m going to sleep. After he did what he did, he went into that place. If you believe, you enter into that place; that is the rest Christ promises to those that are heavy laden.

“Although the works were finished from the foundation of the world. For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” A certain place. When you celebrate the sabbath, the day of rest, the Lord’s day, it is talking about paradise. When Christ says he is Lord of the sabbath, he is saying, I am Lord of paradise, I am king, I am ruler; that rest is mine; that place was created for me.

“And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.” My rest: my city, my country. “They to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief”: many of our forefathers did not enter in because they did not believe. “To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.”

“There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” That rest for the people of God is the kingdom. “For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works”: when we cease from all the labors and works we are doing on this earth, we enter into the Lord’s rest.

sense.text: “Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle.” Peter’s tabernacle is his body. When you read about tabernacles, it is not just talking about the booths we dwell in; it also means this body, this flesh we have. “Even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me”: Christ told him he was going to die.

“That ye may be able after my decease to have these things always in remembrance”: after I die and put off this tabernacle. That is how you put off this tabernacle: this flesh has to die. Scripture calls it transfiguration.

Tonight is the beginning of the feast of tabernacles, Sukkot, a Hebrew word that means to dwell in booths, in a booth tent. “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.” We are in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.

Some of you think it is just about us dwelling in booths. There is much more to it than that.
“On the first day shall be an holy convocation”: the first day is holy.
“On the eighth day shall be an holy convocation unto you”: the eighth day is holy too. “It is a solemn assembly.” What the first day and the eighth day mean is shown below.

“When ye have gathered in the fruit of the land, ye shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven days: on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath.” Something is special about the first day and the eighth day.

On the first day we were with the Lord. We were with Adam, and we had our immortal body, our tabernacle from heaven. The Lord had his body, and we had our body. That first day was when there was no sin, and that is why it is holy.

The eighth day is when the Most High touches down. On the eighth day this flesh has to go, and we all get back our tabernacle from heaven. On the first day we had our immortal body, and on the last day, the eighth day, we get it back.

“And ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees”: good trees, the best boughs, real good, to build the booth and dwell in it. “Branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and ye shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days.”

A bough is the large thick limb of the tree that grows out and branches off from the shaft of the tree. It is not the leaves or the small branches. Those goodly boughs represent something very heavy. The goodly boughs that were part of Adam and got cut off are us in our immortal body. That is why the Lord tells us to take the goodly boughs, make booths and dwell in them.
“And ye shall keep it a feast unto the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations”. It is a statute forever.

precepts.why:
What do the goodly boughs represent? “Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude; Whom art thou like in thy greatness? Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar”. The Lord is about to compare Pharaoh to someone, and he is giving us a clue about the beginning.

“Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches: for his root was by great waters. The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him”. The garden of God: Pharaoh is being compared to Adam, who was in the garden of God. “The fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.” “All the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” Everyone there envied Adam.

The point is the boughs and the branches. They are the righteous that were there with Adam, the elect, the brothers and sisters that were with Adam and had an immortal body. Adam was the tree, and all the boughs and branches are his children with their angelic bodies on.

“I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen”: the mighty one of the heathen is Satan. “I have driven him out for his wickedness”: Adam was cast out of paradise. “Upon the mountains and in all the valleys his branches are fallen”: his branches that fell are us, who were there with Adam in the beginning ruling this earth. We all fell. “And his boughs are broken”: those goodly boughs broken off are us. When we celebrate tabernacles, it is really going into the angelic body we had. “All the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow”: everybody stopped following him.

“All that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men”. All Adam’s sons that drank water started dying, because before that they had an immortal body. After Adam’s sin we all lost that tabernacle, that immortal, spiritual, angelic body, and were cast down to be born in this flesh on the earth, living among men. The water came from the Father to Adam, and from Adam to us. That is what Israel means, that have power with God: we were there with Christ in the beginning with our heavenly tabernacles, and because Adam sinned we all died and are in this flesh. That is why Christ came and died, correcting what was done in the beginning to redeem us, and why he has so much mercy on us.

“I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed”: the waters that come from the Father stopped flowing to Adam when he sinned, and stopped flowing from Adam to us, so we all died. “And I caused Lebanon to mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted for him.” The trees that fainted and died are us in our immortal tabernacles: all the boughs and branches that were part of that tree, part of Adam, broken off and fallen.

“When I cast him down to hell”: hell here is the earth; Adam was cast down to the earth. “And all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water”, the righteous that were there with Adam, “they also went down into hell with him”. When Adam fell he did not fall by himself. All those branches and all those boughs fell with him and were cut off, because there was no water, and the water is the wisdom of the word of God. That is what tabernacles represent.

“A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things: the entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. That city is paradise, which Adam was kicked out of. “And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.”

“Even so also is Israel’s portion. Because for their sakes I made the world: and when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done. Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail”.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is the old world, when Adam was ruling. The way was wide and sure because the 12 tribes of Israel were there ruling with Adam, all with angelic bodies. Before Adam sinned, we all had an immortal body and were living forever.

“For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world”.

Man was created to be immortal. When Adam sinned, death came to all his sons, and they all lost their immortal body. That is the trees and limbs of Ezekiel 31 withering and dying off.

“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”.

The trees that were drinking water in Ezekiel 31, the trees of righteousness, are us, the Israelites. The Lord is the one that planted us.

“For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” The earthly house of this tabernacle is this fleshly body; dissolved means it dies. We have another tabernacle not made with hands, not made of the earth: an eternal body, an eternal tabernacle, in the heavens.

The goodly boughs we build the booth with represent the tabernacles we have in the heavens, that body, that glorious garment.

“For in this we groan”: in this body, which is subject to sin, weak and flimsy. “Earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”: we want back the body we lost after Adam’s sin in the beginning, those goodly boughs and goodly branches, that immortal body. That is what we are working for.

“If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked”: without that body we are naked in this flesh. “For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” This mortal body is swallowed up by our getting back our immortal body. So the goodly boughs of the tabernacle are our immortal body.

Why is the first day a sabbath and the eighth day a sabbath? “And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain. And after seven days the world, that yet awaketh not, shall be raised up, and that shall die that is corrupt”.

After seven days is the eighth day. On the eighth day this corrupt body dies, when the Most High touches down. That goes back to flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. On the first day we had our immortal body, and on the eighth day we get back that tabernacle, that body. That is why the first and the eighth days are holy.

“Their glory also will I take unto me, and give these the everlasting tabernacles, which I had prepared for them.”

Brothers, that is what you want: the everlasting tabernacle. The tabernacle you had on the first day, God is going to give back to you on the eighth day, when the Father touches down on the earth. He prepared it for us; that is why Paul said we have a tabernacle in the heavens.

“They shall have the tree of life for an ointment of sweet savour”.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”. The feast of the Lord is tabernacles, and to be sealed is to get back your body. Every brother that gets back his immortal body is sealed. This is the feast of the Lord, where the Lord gives you back your immortal body. That is what tabernacles is really going into.

“Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord.” This feast is about receiving glorious garments, and that glorious garment is the heavenly tabernacle. “Shut up those of thine that are clothed in white”: the white robe is your immortal body, your heavenly tabernacle. On the eighth day, when the Father returns, everybody gets it back, those “which have fulfilled the law of the Lord”: those that kept God’s laws get back the body lost in the beginning.

“Thy people, which have been called from the beginning, may be hallowed.” We were there in the beginning, on the first day that was holy, when there was no sin. Hallowed means we will be holy again when we get back our immortal body.

“I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number”: that great people is the children of Israel, when the Father comes. A young man “of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns”.

“Sir, what are these?” That is the same thing John asked. Why do they look like that? Because they have on their immortal body, clothed in white; they got back their tabernacle from heaven. “These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God”. The mortal clothing is this body, and this is where Paul got all of this from. We put off this mortal body and get back the immortal body we had in the beginning, lost after Adam’s sin.

“Now are they crowned, and receive palms.” “It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord.” Brothers, you have to stand stiffly for the name of the Lord; don’t let nothing shake you in this truth. Ezra saw the Father return and all of us get back our heavenly tabernacle.

This is the same thing Ezra saw. “A great multitude, which no man could number”, and Ezra called that great multitude Israel, Zion. They “stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”. The white robes are our tabernacle from heaven, our heavenly body, angelic body.

“Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand”: these are the saints sealed before the destruction takes place. “After this” is a span of time: after they are all sealed, the destruction takes place, Christ comes and destroys the nations, and we rule for a thousand years. Then it jumps into the future, after the thousand years.

“Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.” The one on the throne is the Father. God’s kingdom has come on the earth, the kingdom we pray for, after Christ delivers the kingdom to the Father, and we all have our white robes. The angels stand round about the throne, the elders and the four beasts worship God, and at this time there is no heathen on the earth: just the 12 tribes of Israel, with God’s kingdom on the earth. “Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever.”

“What are these which are arrayed in white robes?” Isn’t that the same thing Ezra said? Those white robes represent your heavenly tabernacles, your immortal body. “These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple”: we will serve the Father.

That is why Paul said flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. When the authority is given to God, there will be no flesh and blood; there will be an end to mankind when the fire comes on the earth. Those that were righteous get back their angelic body and are equal to angels. There will be no more flesh.

“And he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them. They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more”. “For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters”: we get back the water we were cut off from in the beginning, in Ezekiel 31. “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.”

“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” This is the kingdom of God coming on the earth.

“Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people”. Everything read before goes into the tabernacle of God being with men: everybody has on their white robe, and the Father dwells with us. That is what we pray for: thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth. But for that to happen we all have to get back our white robes, our tabernacles from the heavens.

“And God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” God himself, because the one we are dealing with right now is his Son, Christ. “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death”, because we got back our tabernacle from heaven.
